alex k: Heads-up: I triggered a perf regression in nightly for a customer workload using FlashAttention v2 causal path. Small heads (h=16) sequences ~512 show 20-30% slowdown vs yesterday. anyone seen this?
maria z: ugh. can you paste the perf trace?
alex k: pasted below — it's the kernel selector flipping to sdpa_v3 fallback after kv-prefetch step. selector log: `kernel=flash_v2->probe(sdpa_v3)->fallback(causal_slowpath)`
chris p: do we have a repro microbenchmark?
alex k: yes, ran on sm86 box. microbench command: ```
# repro
python -m bench.runtime_runner --model=gpt-small --seq=512 --heads=16 --batch=4 --causal
```
irene: interesting — small head dims can break tile alignment for flash kernels and push us into slower matmul path. but sdpa_v3 fallback shouldn't be slower for causal normally.
maria z: can we get the KV cache warmup behavior? I suspect prefetch/hint logic is probing and warming KV which induces extra kernel picks for first few tokens. alex, does the reg reproduce after warmup?
alex k: good call. after 64 tokens into the stream perf returns to expected. so it's the initial window. logs show repeated kernel probes during first 8 steps.
benchmarks-bot: nightly-run: gpt-small h=16 seq=512 batch=4 causal: baseline(2026-03-17)=120ms/token, current=150ms/token (25% regression)
chris p: likely interplay of kernel-probing hysteresis + kv-prefetch. our autotuner currently uses a single probe per (seqlen,headdim,arch) but we allow immediate reprobing if runtime shape changes. that might be too aggressive during kv-warmup when prefix caching rewrites shapes.
irene: suggested interim fix: add a short hysteresis window (e.g., skip reprobing for N steps after a probe for same route) and hold onto previous kernel for at least M tokens unless latency exceeds threshold.
maria z: can we test M=32, N=4? low enough to recover but should avoid thrash. also maybe avoid prefetch-triggered reprobing: prefetch should warm KV asynchronously and not change kernel pick decisions.
alex k: try patch: `kernel_picker.hysteresis_tokens = 32; probe_cooldown_steps = 4; ignore_prefetch_shape_changes = true`
chris p: ran quick local with patch on sm86: repro microbench now shows 125ms/token initial, and returns to 118ms after warmup. still slightly worse than baseline but within noise.
maria z: good. let's capture flamegraph of first 16 tokens pre/post patch. alex can you upload?
alex k: attached snippet of cpu/gpu timeline (trimmed): ```
0-2 tokens: probe(sdpa_v3) -> launch slowpath
2-8 tokens: repeated probes, kernel thrash
8-32 tokens: stable flash_v2
>32 tokens: steady-state optimal
```
chris p: that matches. Also noticed that on sm80 the headstride compute (pack alignment for h=16) differs and our tile-compat test returned false prefetch because of padded stride. could add a headstride-aware compatibility check that tolerates small padding for flash kernels.
irene: agree. propose three changes: 1) hysteresis cooldown, 2) ignore prefetch-only shape delta, 3) headstride-tolerance in tile matcher.  prioritize 1 and 2 for hotfix.
maria z: any risk to accuracy or memory from headstride tolerance? if we allow slightly padded strides we must ensure kernel can handle it without OOB memory reads. add runtime guard to fallback if out-of-bounds.
achris p: typo — chris :) runtime guard is cheap. i'll add a check in tile matcher: `if (stride_padding <= 8) accept_with_guard` and GPU kernel will assert safe range in debug builds.
alex k: timeline for hotfix? customers impacted, rolling back to previous runtime is heavy.
maria z: make hotfix branch, small patch set. bench + canary on infra-qa for 2 hours. if green, push canary then prod.
benchmarks-bot: perf-check queued on infra-qa (sm86, sm80) — will report in ~30m
irene: also log note: we should add a metric for "kernel-thrash-events" when selector flips kernel >2 times within 8 tokens for same request id. helps detect this class of regressions faster.
alex k: added ticket: INF-4932 "kernel thrash metric + hysteresis default"
maria z: thanks. I'll own rollout. @deploy-bot can you stage the canary job after bench success?
deploy-bot: scheduled canary job `canary/flash-picker-hysteresis` pending perf-check success. :rocket:
chris p: one more thought — quantify cost of probe. if probe cost > X% latency we should prefer conservative policy for low batch sizes. maybe tie probe aggressiveness to batch size and latency targets.
alex k: agreed. let's follow up with a short experiment: vary probe frequency across batch in bench harness. I'll open a separate thread for that.
maria z: perfect. thanks team :thumbsup:
